To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
thrombin is a key regulator of vascular smooth muscle cell biology and its effects are regulated by vasodilating prostaglandins.

thrombin binding sites are up-regulated upon vascular injury and that their activation is regulated by vasodilator prostaglandins, which may be of clinical importance in atherosclerosis and related conditions.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of thrombin responsiveness in human SMC, with a special emphasis on the role of vasodilatory PGs.
the identification of novel thrombin receptors, their regulation by vasodilation, and their function in vascular SMC.
the role of thrombin receptors in vascular SMC, their expression and regulation by prostaglandins, and their contribution to vascular tissue remodelling.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
vasodilatory PGs, via their ability to regulate thrombin binding sites in vascular smooth muscle cell, may play a role in vascular repair after vessel injury.

thrombin is a key player in vascular remodelling and that the balance between its pro- and antithrombotic actions is regulated by the local prostacyclin/thromboxane balance and that the latter is controlled in part by the local prostaglandin balance.
the thrombin system is an important mediator of vascular SMC activation and tissue remodelling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
thrombin and vasodilatory PGs act antagonistically in vascular SMC to control tissue remodelling.
thrombin receptors are important in SMC function and their expression is regulated by vasodilators.
thrombin receptors in vascular SMC are functionally regulated by vasodilator prostaglandins, and this is likely to be clinically relevant in atherosclerosis and related disorders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
thrombin receptors in vascular SMC are regulated in an opposing way by the two major vasodilatory prostanoid receptors EP4 (PGI2) and FP (PGE2).
thrombin and its receptors in SMC have a role beyond hemostasis and that vasodilatory PGE2/PIGI2 are able to regulate this activity.
thrombin is a potent mitogen for vascular SMC, and its effects are modulated by vasodilating prostaglandins.
